label: Boot, recovery and stop screens
behaviour: Screens drawn before Windows starts, while it restarts or stops, and by the recovery environment; full screen, no desktop session.

label: Restarting screen
behaviour: Black after the session closes: a dotted spinner with a one-word label under it, both centred, until the firmware takes over.

label: Spinner
behaviour: Dots running round a circle, centred above the middle of the screen; the bounds are the dots seen in 5 frames, so the full circle can reach a little further.

label: Label
behaviour: A text slot of 10 characters in small bold white, centred under the spinner.

label: Boot logo
behaviour: Black in the firmware's own mode (1024x768 on the reference machine), the firmware's logo and Windows' spinner under it; positions are fractions of that screen, which no profile governs.

label: Firmware logo
behaviour: The logo the firmware publishes in its boot graphics table, drawn as it is, centred at 50% across and 50% down; 18% of the screen wide.

label: Spinner
behaviour: A solid arc turning round a circle below the logo, not the Restarting screen's dots; the arc seen in 4 frames in this mode sits centred at 50% across and 78% down. It keeps turning alone once Windows sets the display's own mode, where the arc seen in 11 frames sits centred at 50% across and 78% down at 1920x1080.

label: Boot manager menu
openedBy: Power on, when the boot manager lists more than one entry
behaviour: Blue, the title at the top left, a countdown line, one tile per boot entry named by its description, and a link to the options at the bottom.

label: Choices
behaviour: Tiles in columns of three, read down the first column then the next; arrow keys move the focus, Enter takes it.

label: First entry
behaviour: A 110 px square of the lighter blue with a white line icon, the name beside it at its top; focus draws a white rectangle round tile and text.

label: Second entry
behaviour: A 110 px square of the lighter blue with a white line icon, the name beside it at its top; focus draws a white rectangle round tile and text.

label: Countdown
behaviour: A text slot naming the default entry and the seconds left, counting down from the boot manager's timeout (30 in this walk).

label: Change defaults or choose other options
behaviour: A text link near the bottom left; Tab focuses it with a dotted rectangle, Enter opens the options page.

label: Stop the countdown
behaviour: A key press (Down in this walk) removes the countdown line; the menu then waits for a choice.

label: Move between entries
behaviour: Arrow keys move the focus up and down the tiles.

label: Focus the options link
behaviour: Tab moves the focus from the tiles to the link and back.

label: Start the focused entry
behaviour: Enter starts the focused entry or opens the focused link.

label: Boot manager options
openedBy: Change defaults or choose other options
behaviour: The same blue page with a back button: the first two tiles name a setting with its current value under it, and the third opens the recovery environment, with a line naming what it holds.

behaviour: A circled arrow left of the title; Backspace does the same.

behaviour: An intro line and a bulleted list of what the restart lets you change, then a Restart button; no tiles.

label: What it changes
behaviour: Small bullets with one line each, from low-resolution video to automatic restart after a failure.

label: Restart
behaviour: A small outlined button; Enter restarts into the numbered menu.

label: Startup Settings menu
openedBy: Restart on the Startup Settings page
behaviour: A text menu on the recovery blue in the firmware's mode (1024x768): title, an instruction, nine numbered lines centred at 37% across and 46% down, and two footer lines; positions are fractions of that screen.

label: Numbered options
behaviour: One line each, the number first; the number or function key of that line takes it.

label: Enable debugging
behaviour: Line 1, centred at 26% across and 30% down.

label: Enable boot logging
behaviour: Line 2, centred at 27% across and 34% down.

label: Enable low-resolution video
behaviour: Line 3, centred at 30% across and 38% down.

label: Enable Safe Mode
behaviour: Line 4, centred at 26% across and 42% down.

label: Enable Safe Mode with Networking
behaviour: Line 5, centred at 33% across and 46% down.

label: Enable Safe Mode with Command Prompt
behaviour: Line 6, centred at 36% across and 50% down.

label: Disable driver signature enforcement
behaviour: Line 7, centred at 34% across and 54% down.

label: Disable early launch anti-malware protection
behaviour: Line 8, centred at 37% across and 57% down.

label: Disable automatic restart after failure
behaviour: Line 9, centred at 34% across and 61% down.

label: Choose an option
behaviour: The page's hint line names the number keys and F1 to F9; 4 started Safe mode in this walk.

label: More options
behaviour: Named by the first footer line, for more options; not taken in this walk.

label: Return to Windows
behaviour: Named by the second footer line, to return to the operating system; not taken in this walk.

label: Safe mode desktop
behaviour: The desktop on black with the basic display driver (1024x768 on the reference machine), after sign-in; positions are fractions of that screen.

label: Safe Mode marks
behaviour: The two words in small white text in each corner, over the wallpaper; the bottom pair sits just above the taskbar, which is 48 px tall here. Each mark's size is on its own record.

label: Top left mark
behaviour: In the screen's top left corner; 53 by 9 px at 1024x768.

label: Top right mark
behaviour: In the screen's top right corner; 53 by 9 px at 1024x768.

label: Bottom left mark
behaviour: In the screen's bottom left corner, just above the taskbar; 53 by 9 px at 1024x768.

label: Bottom right mark
behaviour: In the screen's bottom right corner, just above the taskbar; 53 by 9 px at 1024x768.

label: Build line
behaviour: The product name and full build string in one small white line centred at 50% across and 1% down, at the top edge.

label: Stop error screen
openedBy: A stop error (here a non-maskable interrupt from the host)
behaviour: Black in the firmware's mode (1024x768 here), no icon or code image: a message, a progress line and a stop code line; the machine restarted by itself within seconds.

label: Message
behaviour: A text slot of 52 characters in one line, centred at 50% across and 48% down.

label: Progress
behaviour: A text slot of a percentage and one word, centred at 50% across and 57% down; its text stayed the same in the 4 frames compared.

label: Stop code
behaviour: A small text slot with a label, the stop code's name and its number in hex, centred at 50% across and 96% down, near the bottom edge.

label: Stop error shown for

measure.readBy: host frame times, stop-2 to stop-6

behaviour: The span between the host's times for the first exact frame with the stop error and the first exact frame without it; each time is taken as its frame is saved, so this is the span observed, not a bound on the screen's own; with the small memory dump this walk sets.

label: Startup Repair progress
behaviour: A restart to the firmware's logo with a short label centred at 50% across and 84% down, then, at the display's mode, the logo again with a spinner and a label below it, on black.

label: Repair failed
openedBy: Startup Repair, when it cannot repair the PC; the reason shown in this walk, which runs with no network, is that it could not connect to the network
behaviour: Black, centred text: what happened, how to go on, and two smaller white lines with the reason and the log file's path.

label: Message
behaviour: A text slot of 56 characters in one line.

label: Instruction
behaviour: A text slot of 51 characters naming Enter and a click.

label: Details
behaviour: Two smaller white lines: the reason and the log file's path.

label: Show other recovery options
behaviour: Enter or a click opens More recovery options.

label: More recovery options
openedBy: Enter on the repair failed screen
behaviour: The recovery environment's first page after a failed repair: a cloud recovery tile replaces Use a device and Use another operating system, and Turn off sits beside Continue.
